name: Religare Enterprises Ltd
title: Religare Enterprises Ltd - 532915 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Holding-company call with no capacity or pricing data; Care GWP up 24% to INR11,417 crores and combined ratio 101.4%, but the demerger structure and promoter stake questions went unanswered.

triggers.label: Care GWP up 24% to INR11,417 crores
triggers.quote: The company delivered a top line of INR11,417 crores on a full premium basis, reflecting 24% growth while retail health grew by 34%.

summary.headline: Religare Q4 FY26 consolidated total income INR2,473 crores and FY26 PAT INR73.16 crores; Care Health GWP up 24% to INR11,417 crores for FY26.
summary.overview: Management framed FY26 as the move from recovery to rebuilding, citing a reconstituted board, new CEOs at Care, RFL, RBL and RHFL, and fresh capital of about INR1,500 crores raised at REL level. Care Health (significant subsidiary) crossed INR10,000 crores GWP and INR500 crores PBT on n basis, with Ind AS PBT of INR519 crores after a INR64 crores equity mark-to-market loss. Religare Finvest returned to profit (FY26 PAT INR139 crores, Q4 INR89 crores), while Religare Broking and Housing Finance remain small, with HFC still loss-making. A demerger is proposed to split the lending/broking business into RFL, leaving REL as a pure-play Care holding company; the call's Q&A focused heavily on the holding-company structure, promoter stake and the 26% IRDAI threshold, which management largely left open.

segments.name: Care Health Insurance
segments.commentary: FY26 GWP INR11,417 crores (24% growth), retail health up 34%; AUM INR10,944 crores; 6.7% industry share, 11.6% retail health share. Solvency 1.68 (1.70 ex-MTM); claim settlement ratio 97%.

segments.name: Religare Finvest (RFL)
segments.commentary: Middle-layer NBFC with core SME book about INR60 crores and surplus funds above INR590 crores; NNPA about 0.8%, CRAR 261%, NOF INR821 crores, collection efficiency about 98%. FY26 total income INR121.9 crores vs INR75.4 crores.

segments.name: Religare Broking (RBL)
segments.commentary: Q4 total income INR98 crores (up 18% YoY), PBT up 79% to INR12.9 crores. Full-year cash ADTV down 20%, active NSE clients down about 2% to 245,000; net worth INR376 crores.

segments.name: Religare Housing Finance (RHFL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR243 crores (70% home loans, 30% LAP), average ticket INR10-11 lakhs, about 15 branches in 8 states, CRAR about 130%. Q4 revenue INR7.9 crores, GNPA 3.5%, NNPA 2.5%; Q4 loss INR3.6 crores.

guidance_outlook: Care: combined ratio expected to move toward 100% within about 2 years, driven by renewal-cost operating leverage rather than claims; management declined to confirm a profit figure of INR700-800 crores.
Care: growth framed as beating industry; management gave an 18-24% range for sustainable growth over 3-4 years.
RFL: NBFC to launch multiline secured and unsecured products over the next couple of quarters, subject to technology build-out.
RHFL: expected to reach profitability in 12-18 months; ticket size to stay below about INR15 lakhs.

Capital: INR1,500 crores raised at REL level, of which INR600 crores to Care (INR256 crores already infused), INR250 crores to RHFL, INR200 crores to RBL and about INR375 crores general corporate purpose.
Demerger: REL shareholders to receive 1 RFL share per REL share; no timeline given for a clean Care share structure or a further scheme.
capex_capacity: Care: investment book up over INR2,500 crores vs March 2025 with leverage at 4.07x; 93% of book in bonds and G-Secs, 6% in AA-rated instruments.
Care: about 4.11 lakh agents after adding about 50,000 in the year; 239 corporate agents and bancassurance tie-ups; 96% of policies issued digitally.
RFL: IT platform refurbishment underway; no legacy ALM mismatches, balance sheet described as debt-free.
RHFL: comprehensive IT transformation under way; plans to build branch infrastructure as capital arrives.
RBL: technology upgrade of core trading platform and mobile app, including AI initiatives; about 1 million registered clients and 2.5 lakh active.
demand_pricing: Industry retail health grew about 30% in H2 FY26 after GST exemption on individual health policies; Care retail grew 40% in Oct-Mar vs 27% in H1.
Care Q4 retail grew 37% YoY on full-premium basis; agency channel 42% of GWP vs 40% prior year; retail mix 66% on n basis.
Care operated under three accounting bases: n basis PBT INR539 crores, Ind AS INR519 crores, 1/n basis INR18 crores (only six months in prior year on 1/n).
RBL: brokerage up 41% and interest income up 44% in Q4; client funding book up 75% YoY; derivative turnover up 61% YoY in Q4 but cash ADTV down 20% for FY.
RFL interest income rose from INR18.2 crores to INR40.6 crores in the quarter, driven by collections and recoveries.

qa_highlights.question: How can the holding-company discount be avoided given rising promoter stake and Care being a subsidiary of a listed entity?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Lamba said promoters rose about 4% via open market and should reach about 34% after warrant conversion; the current structure is the right step for now and further steps will be evaluated, with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the promoters reach the IRDAI 26% threshold in Care, and can the scheme be amended?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not want to amend the scheme, a subsequent scheme may come at an appropriate time, reaching 26% is 'speculative', and no decision has been taken on other partners such as Kedaara or Anuj Gulati.

qa_highlights.question: What is Care's likely profit trajectory as the combined ratio falls?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Shah said the combined ratio will fall toward 100% in about 2 years through operating leverage; he declined to put a profit figure on it and said Care measures itself only on the combined ratio.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NBFC growth plan and capital deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Karthik Srinivasan (new RFL CEO, joined that week) said the goal is a multiline NBFC mixing secured and unsecured products, with a tech build period before a fast pan-India scale-up; no product or yield targets given.

qa_highlights.question: When will RFL and RHFL disburse and what are their targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Pankaj Rathi said RHFL disburses about INR10 crores a month; no multi-year target was given, but growth will start gradually once first-round capital is deployed.

qa_highlights.question: Is leadership complete and when will the businesses turn profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Lamba said CXO and CEO roles are largely filled, with a CEO for RHFL still being hired and CTOs to follow; RFL and RBL already profitable, while RHFL needs 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Lakshmi Vilas Bank FD recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Lamba said the matter is sub judice; legal proceedings have been started in the Delhi High Court to recover an FD taken from RFL, with no timeline or amount stated.

risks_watch: Holding-company discount and unresolved path to a clean Care share structure; promoters at about 30.3%, about 34% post-warrant conversion, versus the 26% IRDAI threshold; warrants convert by March 2027.
Care Ind AS profit sensitivity to equity mark-to-market (INR64 crores loss in Q4) and solvency at 1.68.
RHFL remains loss-making with GNPA at 3.5%; RFL NBFC has only about INR60 crores of core book, so the lending ramp is unproven.
RBL active client base is falling (down 2% for NSE active clients, down 5% for unique traded clients) and cash turnover fell 20% in FY26.
Recovery of the LVB FD is in litigation with no timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Care's growth and profitability and on RFL's liquidity, but noticeably evasive on the holding-company structure, promoter stake path and reverse-merger questions, repeatedly deferring to 'an appropriate time'. Forward targets for the new NBFC and HFC businesses were largely qualitative.
key_quotes: We moved from recovery to rebuilding with significant progress across leadership, governance, capital availability and regulatory response.
I think the increase has been to the tune of roughly 4%. And post conversion of the warrants, assuming everybody converts their warrants, I mean, promoters should be close to about 34%.

We don't want to amend the scheme. Whether a subsequent scheme can be done, when it can be done, we shall see at an appropriate time. Now whether we can increase our stake to 26%, that is speculative.
So just our NBFC is already reporting profit. Our broking business is already reporting profit. Our HFC is the only one that is not repor ting profit. I think maybe give it another 12 to 18 months.

growth.why: Management guided Care growth of 18-24% over 3-4 years and a combined ratio near 100% in about 2 years, backed mainly by retail demand (retail up 34%, Q4 retail up 37%) and renewal-cost operating leverage, with no specific capacity additions, order book or timelines beyond general statements.

mgmt.note: New CEOs appointed at Care, RFL, RBL and RHFL during FY26 with a reconstituted board; management framed FY26 as the shift from recovery to rebuilding.
initiatives: RFL multiline secured and unsecured products over next couple of quarters
